plan.contextChunk: This figure pairs a titration curve for alanine with the structures present at each stage along it. The plot area is tinted pale blue and gridded; the vertical axis is labeled "pH" and runs from 0 to 12 with labeled ticks every 2 units, and the horizontal axis reads "Equivalents of HO-" and runs from 0.0 to 2.0 with ticks every 0.5. A magenta curve climbs from the bottom left in two legs, each a shallow buffering stretch followed by a steep rise, the two joined by a near-vertical jump at one equivalent. Three points on the curve are marked with an x and annotated: "pKa1 = 2.34" at 0.5 equivalent, "Isoelectric point = 6.01" at 1.0 equivalent, and "pKa2 = 9.69" at 1.5 equivalents. Thin arrows run from five positions on the curve out to bracketed structural formulas at the right, drawn with the ammonium nitrogen in magenta and the neutral amine nitrogen in blue: at the foot, the fully protonated cation with an intact carboxylic acid; at pKa1, a bracketed pair of that cation and the zwitterion; at the isoelectric point, the zwitterion alone; at pKa2, a bracketed pair of zwitterion and carboxylate anion; and at the top, the fully deprotonated anion. Aligning each structure with its own stretch of curve shows which species dominates over each pH range and pins down the pH at which the molecule carries no net charge.

interactionPlan.concept: Titrating alanine with hydroxide converts it stepwise from a fully protonated cation through the neutral zwitterion to the carboxylate anion, with the pKa values at half-equivalence points and the isoelectric point at one full equivalent.
elements: Pale blue tinted plot area with light gray gridlines
Vertical axis labeled 'pH', range 0 to 12, labeled ticks every 2 units
Horizontal axis labeled 'Equivalents of HO⁻', range 0.0 to 2.0, labeled ticks every 0.5

Magenta titration curve rising in two sigmoidal legs: shallow buffering near pH 2.34, near-vertical jump at 1.0 equivalent, second buffering plateau near pH 9.69, steep rise toward pH 11.5 at 2.0 equivalents
Black 'x' marker at (0.5, 2.34) with annotation 'pKa1 = 2.34' and curved leader arrow
Black 'x' marker at (1.0, 6.01) with annotation 'Isoelectric point = 6.01' and curved leader arrow
Black 'x' marker at (1.5, 9.69) with annotation 'pKa2 = 9.69' and curved leader arrow
Movable circular marker on the curve tied to the equivalents slider, with pH readout callout

Structure panel: bracketed 50:50 pair at pKa1 — cation + zwitterion, joined by '+'
Structure panel: bracketed zwitterion H3N⁺-CH(CH3)-COO⁻ alone
Structure panel: bracketed 50:50 pair at pKa2 — zwitterion + anion, joined by '+'
Structure panel: bracketed fully deprotonated anion H2N-CH(CH3)-COO⁻ (neutral amine N in blue)
Thin black leader arrows from five curve positions (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 equivalents) to their structures
Net-charge overlay badges (+1, 0, −1) and colored charge markers usable in the charge view
Legend/key noting magenta = protonated ammonium nitrogen, blue = neutral amine nitrogen

interactions.label: Equivalents of HO⁻ added
interactions.teaches: How pH responds unevenly to added base — flat buffering regions around each pKa and a sharp jump at the equivalence point — and which alanine species dominates at each stage.

interactions.label: Right-panel view
interactions.teaches: That the zwitterion, though it carries both a + and a − site, has zero net charge, which is exactly why pH 6.01 is the isoelectric point.

Clicking pKa1, the isoelectric point, or pKa2 shows that half-equivalence points hold a 50:50 mixture of two species (pH = pKa) while the full equivalence point holds essentially a single neutral zwitterion.

demo_steps.title: Start: fully protonated cation
demo_steps.narration: With no base added, alanine sits at pH ~0.3 as the cation: protonated ammonium and intact carboxylic acid, net charge +1.

demo_steps.title: First buffering region: pKa1
demo_steps.narration: At 0.5 equivalent the carboxylic acid is half neutralized; the solution holds equal amounts of cation and zwitterion and the pH equals pKa1 = 2.34.

demo_steps.title: Equivalence point: the zwitterion
demo_steps.narration: One full equivalent converts nearly all the COOH to COO⁻. The pH leaps through the steep region and settles at 6.01, where the zwitterion dominates.

demo_steps.title: Why 6.01 is the isoelectric point
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the net-charge view: the +1 ammonium and −1 carboxylate cancel, so the dominant species carries zero net charge and will not migrate in an electric field.

demo_steps.title: Second buffering region: pKa2
demo_steps.narration: At 1.5 equivalents the ammonium group is half deprotonated; zwitterion and anion are present 50:50 and pH = pKa2 = 9.69.

demo_steps.title: End: fully deprotonated anion
demo_steps.narration: By 2.0 equivalents both acidic protons are gone, leaving the neutral blue amine and carboxylate anion with net charge −1 near pH 11.5.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Each flat stretch of the curve is a 50:50 buffer where pH equals a pKa, and the isoelectric point sits midway between the two pKa values — the one pH where alanine exists almost entirely as the zero-net-charge zwitterion.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Wide landscape layout: titration plot occupies the left ~45% of the canvas, structure panel the right ~55%. Plot area filled pale blue (#ddeffa) with thin gray gridlines at every labeled tick; axes black with 'pH' rotated at left (0–12, ticks every 2) and 'Equivalents of HO⁻' beneath (0.0–2.0, ticks every 0.5). Curve is a thick magenta/crimson (#e8186c) double-sigmoid: rises steeply from pH ~0.3 at zero equivalents, flattens through pH 2.34 near 0.5 eq, bends upward and jumps near-vertically at 1.0 eq passing through pH 6.01, flattens again through 9.69 at 1.5 eq, then climbs to ~11.5 at 2.0 eq. Three black 'x' markers with small curved leader arrows and labels 'pKa1 = 2.34', 'Isoelectric point = 6.01', 'pKa2 = 9.69'. Right panel stacks five bracketed structural formulas top-to-bottom in the order anion, zwitterion+anion pair, zwitterion, cation+zwitterion pair, cation — each connected by a thin black arrow to its matching point on the curve. Draw skeletal condensed formulas: H3N⁺ in magenta for protonated nitrogen, H2N in blue for neutral amine, CH3 on a vertical bond below the alpha carbon, C=O with O above and O⁻ or OH to the right (acidic H in magenta). In net-charge view, replace/overlay each structure with large colored charge badges (+1 red, 0 gray, −1 blue) and tint the charged sites. Active slider position shows a filled dot on the curve plus a dashed drop-line to both axes with a live pH readout; clicked landmarks glow with a highlight ring and their structure panel gets a highlighted border while others dim.

authoredContext:
Solving the two simultaneous equations gives [HA] = 0.83 and [A–] = 0.17. In other words, at pH = 9.00, 83% of alanine molecules in a 1.00 M solution are neutral (zwitterionic) and 17% are deprotonated. Similar calculations can be done at other pH values and the results plotted to give the titration curve shown in the figure.

Look carefully at the titration curve in the figure. In acid solution, the amino acid is protonated and exists primarily as a cation. In basic solution, the amino acid is deprotonated and exists primarily as an anion. In between the two is an intermediate pH at which the amino acid is exactly balanced between anionic and cationic forms, existing primarily as the neutral, dipolar zwitterion. This pH is called the amino acid’s isoelectric point (pI) and has a value of 6.01 for alanine.

Each leg of the titration curve is calculated separately. The first leg, from pH 1 to 6, corresponds to the dissociation of protonated alanine, H2A+. The second leg, from pH 6 to 11, corresponds to the dissociation of zwitterionic alanine, HA. It’s as if we started with H2A+ at low pH and then titrated with NaOH. When 0.5 equivalent of NaOH is added, the deprotonation of H2A+ is 50% complete; when 1.0 equivalent of NaOH is added, the deprotonation of H2A+ is finished and HA predominates; when 1.5 equivalents of NaOH is added, the deprotonation of HA is 50% complete; and when 2.0 equivalents of NaOH is added, the deprotonation of HA is finished.

A titration curve for alanine, plotted using the Henderson–Hasselbalch equation. Each of the two legs is plotted separately. At pH < 1, alanine is entirely protonated; at pH = 2.34, alanine is a 50: 50 mix of protonated and neutral forms; at pH = 6.01, alanine is entirely neutral; at pH = 9.69, alanine is a 50: 50 mix of neutral and deprotonated forms; at pH > 11.5, alanine is entirely deprotonated.

The figure shows the titration curve for alanine. The x-axis represents equivalents of hydroxide ion and the y-axis represents the pH. It shows isoelectric point and two dissociation constant values.

discrepancies: The rendered output is not a figure at all: the screenshot shows only 'Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'anion')' with a Reload button — no axes, no titration curve, no structures. drawAll() is invoked synchronously from the Chart constructor's first draw, but LMTIP/LMPOP/SPPOP are declared with `var` *after* the Chart is constructed, so SPPOP is undefined when drawPanel does SPPOP[R.id][0] for the first row (id 'anion').

Consequently every source element is missing from the visible output: the pink sigmoidal titration curve, the pale-blue shaded plot region, the 0–2 equivalents x-axis and 0–12 pH y-axis with gridlines, and the three ✕ landmark markers.
All source annotations are absent on screen: 'pKa1 = 2.34', 'Isoelectric point = 6.01', 'pKa2 = 9.69', 'pH', 'Equivalents of HO⁻', and the five bracketed alanine structures with their leader arrows.
The color scheme of the source (magenta curve, magenta H₃N⁺ / blue H₂N lettering, light-blue plot tint) is not visible at all.
Interactions (slider, net-charge toggle, demo stepper, landmark click popups) cannot be exercised because the canvas never paints; the UI panel itself is also not visible in the error state.
evaluation.notes: The code contains a thoughtfully planned, chemically accurate reproduction (pchip curve through the correct pK landmarks, five bracketed alanine structures, stepper/slider/charge toggle), but it throws at first paint because SPPOP/LMTIP/LMPOP are declared after the Chart constructor triggers drawAll, so the delivered artifact is an error message rather than a figure.

⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: The plot area is squeezed into roughly the left third of the canvas (right padding ≈55% reserved for the structure panel), so the titration curve, tick labels and annotation labels all render much smaller relative to the figure than in the source, where the graph occupies about half the width and the annotations are prominent.

The 'Isoelectric point = 6.01' annotation is split onto two lines with an unusually large vertical gap (placed at pH 7.95 and 7.10), so it reads as two separate labels rather than one two-line caption as in the source.

Annotation labels (pKa1 = 2.34, pKa2 = 9.69, Isoelectric point) are noticeably smaller than the axis-title text hierarchy implies and are uncomfortably small at inline size, unlike the source where they are the most prominent text on the plot.

Extra elements not in the source: a colour key strip at the bottom of the panel ('■ protonated N (H₃N⁺)/acidic H ■ neutral amine (H₂N)') and a dark marker dot on the curve at the origin; they are useful but add chrome absent from the original.

Curve stroke in the generated figure is thinner/less bold relative to plot size than the heavy magenta trace of the source, and the origin end of the curve starts at pH ≈0.3 rather than visually touching 0 as in the source.
evaluation.notes: A faithful and conceptually accurate reconstruction of the alanine titration curve with all five bracketed structures, correct landmark ✕ markers and a rich, well-wired set of interactions (slider, net-charge toggle, 6-step demo, clickable curve/structures); the main weaknesses are a cramped plot area and annotation labels that are too small, with the isoelectric-point caption split awkwardly across two widely separated lines.
action_items: Reduce the reserved right padding (currently ~55% of width) so the plot area is closer to the source proportion, and scale annotation font sizes off the overall figure width rather than the shrunken plot dimension so 'pKa1 = 2.34', 'pKa2 = 9.69' and the isoelectric caption read clearly at inline size.
Tighten the two-line 'Isoelectric point = 6.01' label to a single leading (≈1.2× font size apart) so it reads as one caption, and align its leader arrow to the caption block as in the source.
Increase the magenta curve stroke weight relative to the plot and extend/anchor the low-pH end so it visually meets the origin like the source trace.

plan.concept: Titrating alanine with hydroxide converts it stepwise from a fully protonated cation through the neutral zwitterion to the carboxylate anion, with the pKa values at half-equivalence points and the isoelectric point at one full equivalent.
elements: Pale blue tinted plot area with light gray gridlines
Vertical axis labeled 'pH', range 0 to 12, labeled ticks every 2 units
Horizontal axis labeled 'Equivalents of HO⁻', range 0.0 to 2.0, labeled ticks every 0.5

Magenta titration curve rising in two sigmoidal legs: shallow buffering near pH 2.34, near-vertical jump at 1.0 equivalent, second buffering plateau near pH 9.69, steep rise toward pH 11.5 at 2.0 equivalents
Black 'x' marker at (0.5, 2.34) with annotation 'pKa1 = 2.34' and curved leader arrow
Black 'x' marker at (1.0, 6.01) with annotation 'Isoelectric point = 6.01' and curved leader arrow
Black 'x' marker at (1.5, 9.69) with annotation 'pKa2 = 9.69' and curved leader arrow
Movable circular marker on the curve tied to the equivalents slider, with pH readout callout
Structure panel at right: bracketed fully protonated cation H3N⁺-CH(CH3)-COOH (ammonium N in magenta, acidic OH in magenta)
Structure panel: bracketed 50:50 pair at pKa1 — cation + zwitterion, joined by '+'
Structure panel: bracketed zwitterion H3N⁺-CH(CH3)-COO⁻ alone
Structure panel: bracketed 50:50 pair at pKa2 — zwitterion + anion, joined by '+'
Structure panel: bracketed fully deprotonated anion H2N-CH(CH3)-COO⁻ (neutral amine N in blue)
Thin black leader arrows from five curve positions (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 equivalents) to their structures

interactions.label: Equivalents of HO⁻ added
interactions.teaches: How pH responds unevenly to added base — flat buffering regions around each pKa and a sharp jump at the equivalence point — and which alanine species dominates at each stage.

interactions.label: Right-panel view
interactions.teaches: That the zwitterion, though it carries both a + and a − site, has zero net charge, which is exactly why pH 6.01 is the isoelectric point.

Clicking pKa1, the isoelectric point, or pKa2 shows that half-equivalence points hold a 50:50 mixture of two species (pH = pKa) while the full equivalence point holds essentially a single neutral zwitterion.

demo_steps.title: Start: fully protonated cation
demo_steps.narration: With no base added, alanine sits at pH ~0.3 as the cation: protonated ammonium and intact carboxylic acid, net charge +1.

demo_steps.title: First buffering region: pKa1
demo_steps.narration: At 0.5 equivalent the carboxylic acid is half neutralized; the solution holds equal amounts of cation and zwitterion and the pH equals pKa1 = 2.34.

demo_steps.title: Equivalence point: the zwitterion
demo_steps.narration: One full equivalent converts nearly all the COOH to COO⁻. The pH leaps through the steep region and settles at 6.01, where the zwitterion dominates.

demo_steps.title: Why 6.01 is the isoelectric point
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the net-charge view: the +1 ammonium and −1 carboxylate cancel, so the dominant species carries zero net charge and will not migrate in an electric field.

demo_steps.title: Second buffering region: pKa2
demo_steps.narration: At 1.5 equivalents the ammonium group is half deprotonated; zwitterion and anion are present 50:50 and pH = pKa2 = 9.69.

demo_steps.title: End: fully deprotonated anion
demo_steps.narration: By 2.0 equivalents both acidic protons are gone, leaving the neutral blue amine and carboxylate anion with net charge −1 near pH 11.5.

plan.keyInsight: Each flat stretch of the curve is a 50:50 buffer where pH equals a pKa, and the isoelectric point sits midway between the two pKa values — the one pH where alanine exists almost entirely as the zero-net-charge zwitterion.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Wide landscape layout: titration plot occupies the left ~45% of the canvas, structure panel the right ~55%. Plot area filled pale blue (#ddeffa) with thin gray gridlines at every labeled tick; axes black with 'pH' rotated at left (0–12, ticks every 2) and 'Equivalents of HO⁻' beneath (0.0–2.0, ticks every 0.5). Curve is a thick magenta/crimson (#e8186c) double-sigmoid: rises steeply from pH ~0.3 at zero equivalents, flattens through pH 2.34 near 0.5 eq, bends upward and jumps near-vertically at 1.0 eq passing through pH 6.01, flattens again through 9.69 at 1.5 eq, then climbs to ~11.5 at 2.0 eq. Three black 'x' markers with small curved leader arrows and labels 'pKa1 = 2.34', 'Isoelectric point = 6.01', 'pKa2 = 9.69'. Right panel stacks five bracketed structural formulas top-to-bottom in the order anion, zwitterion+anion pair, zwitterion, cation+zwitterion pair, cation — each connected by a thin black arrow to its matching point on the curve. Draw skeletal condensed formulas: H3N⁺ in magenta for protonated nitrogen, H2N in blue for neutral amine, CH3 on a vertical bond below the alpha carbon, C=O with O above and O⁻ or OH to the right (acidic H in magenta). In net-charge view, replace/overlay each structure with large colored charge badges (+1 red, 0 gray, −1 blue) and tint the charged sites. Active slider position shows a filled dot on the curve plus a dashed drop-line to both axes with a live pH readout; clicked landmarks glow with a highlight ring and their structure panel gets a highlighted border while others dim.

The 'Isoelectric point = 6.01' caption sits noticeably higher (≈pH 8.2) than in the source (≈pH 6.8–7.2), so its leader arrow travels farther and the label block crowds the pKa2 annotation column.

The narration/step panel and hint text occupy a large fixed right column; at default width this shrinks the figure relative to the source's full-width composition (cosmetic, but it shifts the balance of the plot vs. structure panel).
